newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM GOLD FUTURES END HIGHER, PGMS MOSTLY DOWN.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM GOLD FUTURES END HIGHER, PGMS MOSTLY DOWN.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended higher in quiet trade on Wednesday amid Japan's summer holidays, helped by a strong recovery in bullion prices, traders said.
"We've seen some short covering, though I don't think we can say the gold's downtrend is over," said a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses.
Spot gold was quoted at $328.60/9.00 per ounce at 0710 GMT after hitting a low around $324.80 in New York overnight.
Most platinum group metals (PGMs) continued their slide prompted by Monday's news that a strike at South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd had ended.
Gold futures were unchanged to up five yen per gram higher, helped by bullion's advance.

Most-active benchmark June was up three yen at 1,215 yen. Another trader said: "We might see some funds flowing into gold as the Dow (Jones Industrial Average) started to fall, though upside remains very heavy."
Palladium futures shed between one to six yen per gram, with benchmark June closing down one yen at 698 yen.
Platinum futures were mixed, with the nearby August losing 23 yen while benchmark June added six yen to end at 1,512.
One trader said: "In white metals, you still cannot push down the prices a lot. There're still quite a lot of short positions left."
But another trader said platinum futures could decline as the metal's prices have been pulled up by tightness in the physical palladium market. --- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-6179
